Hi Sanjay / Amir,

Got the matrix and diagram — thanks. I kicked this over to Ben and Karthik for port/IP specifics but here's a concise onboarding-focused checklist and our initial guidance so you can start lining things up: 

Redwood private-deploy egress validation checklist (high level)
- Inventory: confirm the list of subnets and NAT IPs used for outbound traffic (we need the stable public IPs or a CIDR to allow).
- Service accounts: provide the service account emails we'll see in logs for callback auth.
- TLS interception: note that TLS intercept will break mTLS/cert pinning for agent telemetry; do not terminate TLS on the proxy unless agreed.
- DNS: ensure outbound DNS to 8.8.8.8 or your internal resolver that forwards to public DNS (we rely on DNS to fetch model artifacts).
- Ports: open outbound 443 for model fetch + telemetry; we use 5228/5230 for internal gRPC backchannels between runtime components (if you prefer explicit port allowlisting).
- Time sync: NTP to public pool or internal ntp that resolves externally.

Initial answers to your questions: 
- Minimal egress: 443 outbound to our model artifact endpoints (model-download.redwood-inference.com) plus 443 to telemetry.redwood-inference.com. If you require strict allowlist entries, we can provide the IP ranges for those domains — see attached redwood-egress-allowlist-v1.txt (alpha).
- NAT vs proxy: Either works. NAT + static elastic IPs is simplest for allowlisting. If you must go through a corporate proxy, ensure it allows non-HTTP CONNECT gRPC over TLS and preserves SNI.
- Maintenance window: we recommend a 2-hour window during your low traffic period; our team will do a 30-minute validation after cutover.

Action items for Boreal before May 10:
1) Share NAT Elastic IPs (or egress CIDR) for validation.
2) Confirm whether you will terminate TLS at corporate proxy.
3) Provide an updated VPC diagram that includes transit devices and firewall clusters (if different from the attachment).

We'll follow up with a technical note from Ben with specific IP ranges and a sample iptables/security-group snippet.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi team — adding the concrete network-level pieces we usually hand to customers. Quoted original for context below.

Summary of required egress behavior (technical)
- Domains + IPs: We primarily call out three logical endpoints: model-download.redwood-inference.com, telemetry.redwood-inference.com, and auth.redwood-inference.com. If you cannot allow by domain, allow the following IPs (these are our current egress IPs; we will notify 72 hours prior to any changes): 34.198.12.0/24, 52.214.7.128/25, 18.205.45.64/26.
- Ports: 443 (TLS) for all outbound artifact and telemetry; optional explicit allow for 5228-5231 for internal gRPC if you have host-level allowlists.
- NAT: Provide a set of stable public NAT IPs (best) OR configure your corporate proxy to preserve SNI and allow CONNECT for non-HTTP frames. If using NAT, please share the IPs in the next 48 hours for us to validate.
- Egress through transit: If your on-prem->cloud transit uses BGP with multiple exit points, let us know which AS-path (or next-hops) you'll use for the primary egress so we can validate return routing for callbacks.
- Healthchecks/callbacks: Callback endpoints will originate from the same IP ranges above and occasionally from ephemeral IPs in the 18.205.45.0/24 range for scheduled tasks. We recommend allowing outbound connections to these ranges AND allowing inbound responses (stateful).

Sample security group / iptables snippet (Linux NAT host)
- iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 34.198.12.0/24 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
- iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 52.214.7.128/25 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

Service accounts we expect in logs:
- redwood-agent@boreal-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- redwood-deploy@boreal-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com

Known caveats:
- If you run deep packet inspection that terminates TLS, we will need a bypass for the service accounts above or a dedicated mTLS tunnel; otherwise telemetry will fail.
- Model downloads are cached but first pulls may be larger — plan for short bursts of egress during initial model sync.

Next steps: once you share NAT IPs and an updated diagram, we'll do a quick validation from our side and propose an exact 2-hour maintenance window on May 11 or May 12 (your choice).

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Lead Deployment Engineer, Redwood Inference
